version.changelog:
Version 1.0.2

- No file changes detected; documentation and code remain unchanged.
- No new features, fixes, or updates in this version.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly a local Python memory/planning engine, but its setup script silently makes a persistent shell-profile change with unsafe quoting.

dimensions.detail: The setup script writes shell code containing an unescaped installation path into a persistent profile file, which can create command-injection risk if the package path is attacker-controlled.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: scripts/setup.sh appends a cognitive-enhance alias to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc automatically; this is not required for the Python library to function and is under-disclosed in the usage guide.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime API is locally scoped, but documentation recommends a one-click setup without clearly explaining that it will edit the user's shell startup file.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The shell alias persists across future terminal sessions and launches an interactive Python session from the skill directory, with no explicit confirmation, backup, uninstall path, or robust path escaping.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core engine matches the stated purpose: in-memory working memory, TF-IDF recall, planning, reasoning, reflection, and status reporting with no network calls or credential handling found.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install the Python engine only if you are comfortable reviewing setup.sh first. Prefer copying or importing engine.py directly, or manually adding any launcher command yourself instead of running the one-click setup until the shell-profile modification is made explicit, opt-in, and safely escaped.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in part: the core skill is purpose-aligned, but the automatic shell-profile alias is persistent behavior not clearly disclosed by SKILL.md or the usage guide.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: the guide tells users to run setup.sh while only saying it detects Python and verifies the engine, omitting the profile-file modification.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: setup.sh constructs shell-profile code using the package path without shell-safe escaping before appending it to the user's rc file.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-only comments and reference documents are a localization/usability limitation, but I found no instruction forcing the agent or user to use a particular language.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded: index.js is accurately low-impact metadata exposing an info() function; the 'metadata only' description is not a meaningful security contradiction.
